data.name: Musharrif
data.gender_notes: Musharrif is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: One who observes or witnesses. Derived from the Arabic root 'sh-r-f', meaning 'to observe'. In Islamic history, Musharrif refers to those who dedicate themselves to the remembrance of Allah. The name Musharrif carries the meaning “Observer, Watcher” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Musharrif usually hope their child will grow to embody observer, watcher and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name that signifies constant awareness and connection to Allah.
data.etymology: Musharrif belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Observer, Watcher.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Musharrif total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

historical_references.reference: The title 'Musharrif' was given to the ruler of Damascus, Al-Afdal Shahanshah (1061-1095 CE), by the Seljuq Sultan Malik Shah I. The name signified the holder's authority over the 'mashar', or sacred precincts, of Damascus which included the Umayyad Mosque and the tomb of Caliph Umar.
historical_references.context: During the Seljuq Empire in the Middle East.

historical_references.reference: Another notable figure who held the title 'Musharrif' was Sultan Qutbuddin Aibak (1206-1210 CE) of the Slave Dynasty in India. The title symbolized his administrative control over the holy city of Delhi and the mosque complexes, including the Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque.
historical_references.context: During the Slave Dynasty in India.
